headline: NEUTRAL
headline_tag: a month-long slide has Bitcoin testing its 200-week line

action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: Hold the planned budget level. The long-run uptrend still counts, but Bitcoin is down about 10% in a week, about 6% under its 200-day average and only about 1% above its 200-week average, and a Rally watch drop window has been open since 11 November. Lead with trust and education, keep a reserve rather than raising spend, and only speed up after a close back above $73,001 (the 200-day average). This is a budget posture for planning, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($68,388) is about 6% under its 200-day average and 1% above the 200-week.
Up about 9% over 90 days, but down about 17% over the last 30.
The 200-day average ($73,001) is still rising, about 5% over 90 days.
Fear & Greed at 13 (extreme fear); 24 days under the 50-day average ($80,246).
watch: Bitcoin is only about 1% above its 200-week average ($67,711), the last big floor, while many traders are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, which can make a break lower sharper. A close back above $70,500 would steady the week, while a close below $67,711 would turn it clearly down and put $64,506 (the 90-day low) in view.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run picture still leans up, but the short term is weak and Bitcoin is sitting just above its last big floor. Short term, the mood is very fearful: at about $68,388 Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 24 days, sits about 15% below it and about 19% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 13 (extreme fear). US wholesale prices rose at their fastest yearly pace in nearly four years (PANews), keeping worries about higher US interest rates alive. A normal week swings about $4,069, so a close above $70,500 (top of a typical week's swing) would steady things, a close below $67,711 (the 200-week average) would turn the week clearly down, and in between it stays choppy; safety and explainer messaging fits better than any promotion this week.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still show price about 9% higher with most of those days above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 17%, and markets now fully expect a US rate rise at the 8 December Fed meeting (QCP via PANews); news is adding a little, as US exchanges line up for the CFTC's new crypto rules and Korea set a target date for its crypto law. Price is well under its 50-day average, so it must win back $80,246 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. Keep bigger campaign pushes for after the Fed meeting.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but weakly: the 200-day average is still rising (about 5% over 90 days) while price is about 6% under it and about 45% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $73,001 (the 200-day average) again; $67,711 (the 200-week average) is the floor being tested right now, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. A run of closes below the 200-week average would weaken this picture clearly and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.

items.theme: Rate-rise worries pull the whole market down
items.why: US wholesale prices rose 6.5% over the year in October, the fastest pace in nearly four years, and QCP's report says markets now fully expect a US rate rise in December, with the 10-year US bond yield up to about 5.1%. Bitcoin fell below $68,000 and the largest coins fell by similar amounts; the reports point to rate worries rather than any crypto-specific event.

items.why: MANTRA says hackers used a Keplr and Web3Auth wallet key leak to drain user wallets and undo staking, so it paused all unstaking for 7 days; Upbit separately said it will delist MANTRA on 14 December over unresolved security incidents. In India, Unocoin is investigating losses that custodian BitGo says were signed with keys Unocoin itself held.
